title: Discovery: Reliability & Fallbacks with Aurelia Logistics
next_steps: Maya to send SOC2 + security pack
Liam to share proposed Dedicated sizing and pricing
Schedule 1-week perf POC (multi-region) w/ Aurelia infra team
Aurelia to provide sample traffic profile and success criteria
action_items: Maya Chen: Send SOC2 and infra security docs (due 2026-04-02)
Liam Ortiz: Share Dedicated cluster sizing + estimated cost (due 2026-04-06)
Priya Singh: Upload traffic profile and SLA targets to shared drive (due 2026-04-03)

summary: Initial discovery focused on reliability, incident tolerance, and fallback strategies across Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Aurelia wants multi-region failover, predictable SLAs for peak routing, and clarity on data residency/KMS. Agreed to run a 1-week POC for multi-region failover and shared next steps.
transcript: [00:00] Meeting started 2026-03-30 15:00 UTC \u0014 duration ~48m \u0014 Attendees: Maya, Liam, Priya, Ben, Sofia
[00:10] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Maya Chen, AE at Redwood. With me is Liam, our solutions engineer. Quick round robo-intros?
[00:20] Priya: Hi Maya \u0014 Priya Singh, CTO at Aurelia Logistics. We run routing and last-mile logistics in North America, heavy spikes during peak windows.
[00:30] Ben: Ben Martinez, Platform. I own infra and SRE. We're evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private because of both latency and compliance constraints.
[00:42] Sofia: Sofia Reyes, Head of MLOps \u0014 we own models and deployments \u0014 mainly concerned about stateful caches, KV cache persistence, and failover behavior.

[00:55] Maya: Great. Today's goal \u0014 understand your reliability expectations, failure modes, and whether Redwood's Hosted or Dedicated or Private fit. We'll cover multi-region routing, fallbacks, SLA, and operational runbooks.
[01:10] Liam: I'll give a quick overview of our routing & fallback capabilities and then we can drill into scenarios you care about.
[01:20] Maya: Quick question \u0014 what's your timeline for a POC or rollout?
[01:25] Priya: We're hoping to start a POC within 2-3 weeks and decide by end of quarter. Need to show end-to-end failover for peak times.
[01:40] Ben: Also need to validate cost/latency trade-offs. We can't accept >300ms p95 for certain user flows during peaks.
[01:50] Sofia: And we need keys to stay in our KMS \u0014 we cannot export plaintext model data. So KMS/HSM integration is a must for Private or Dedicated options.

[02:05] Liam: Understood. High level: Hosted gives fastest onboarding, Redwood Dedicated provides reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput, and Redwood Private lets you keep control of networking and keys. For reliability we offer multi-region routing, automatic fallback to cheaper/compatible model variants, and capacity tiering with graceful degradation.
[02:20] Priya: Can you expand on 'fallback to compatible model variants' \u0014 what happens to quality?

[02:28] Liam: Sure. We let you define a policy \u0014 priority is: same model version in another region, then a quantized variant, then a smaller model. You can set quality thresholds and auto rollback. If quality drops, we fall back to cached responses or an offline heuristic depending on route.
[02:45] Sofia: When you say "cached responses" \u0014 is that prefix/KV cache? How consistent is that across regions?
[02:52] Liam: It's our prefix and KV cache. For Hosted, caches are region-local; for Dedicated you can enable cross-region replication for hot prefixes. But that introduces replication lag tradeoffs.
[03:10] Ben: Replication lag is a concern \u0014 we need strong consistency for certain real-time decisions. If there's even a second of staleness we might misroute deliveries.

[03:20] Maya: Good to call that out \u0014 so we typically recommend Dedicated with cross-region cache replication for ultra low-staleness, or Private deployed into your VPC with a regional messaging layer if you need sub-second guarantees.
[03:35] Priya: How does multi-region routing actually work? If us-east goes down, do requests automatically go to us-west? What's the detection window?

[03:44] Liam: We use health checks at both infra and service level. For infra failures we detect within ~10-30s depending on check sensitivity; for degraded latency we have policy thresholds you can tune. Then routing switches per policy \u0014 instant re-route to a secondary region with circuit-breaker logic to avoid cascading failures.
[04:00] Priya: 10-30s is okay, but our product team wants to simulate global outage and see how session affinity behaves \u0014 we use KV for session state related to ongoing conversations.

[04:12] Liam: Session affinity is sticky by default for low-latency sessions. For failover we have two options: active-active with state replication, or active-passive with stateless fallbacks. For stateful sessions we recommend active-active Dedicated clusters with cross-region KV replication and conflict resolution rules.
[04:30] Ben: Is cross-region KV replication supported in Hosted?
[04:33] Liam: Not by default. Hosted focuses on single-region performance; for multi-region you'll want Dedicated or Private where you control replication.
[04:40] Priya: Ok. SLA \u0014 what do you guarantee for Hosted vs Dedicated?

[04:45] Maya: Hosted has our standard SLA for availability on the API endpoints \u0014 we publish region-level uptime targets but Dedicated has stronger SLA options tied to reserved capacity. For Dedicated we can provide contractual p95 latency targets on committed capacity, and credits if we miss.
[05:00] Ben: Can you give numbers?

[05:02] Liam: Typical p99 latency targets depend on model and seq length; for Dedicated we design for your workload \u0014 e.g., 150-200ms p95 for standard generator models on c5-sized GPU fleet equivalent. We can run bench tests and commit to a target on the contract.
[05:20] Priya: That's promising. Another question \u0014 how do you handle capacity spikes? We have sudden bursts during promotions and need guaranteed throughput for short windows.

[05:30] Maya: Dedicated supports burst capacity and autoscaling policies. You can configure burst pools or queued requests with rate limiting. For predictable spikes we recommend reserved capacity with overprovision margin or a hybrid with Hosted as fallback.
[05:42] Sofia: Hybrid meaning we route overflow to Hosted? That concerns us for data residency and keys.

[05:48] Liam: We support hybrid routing but you can set data residency rules and KMS constraints: e.g., requests with sensitive PII only route to Dedicated/Private; less-sensitive traffic can overflow to Hosted. Hosted cannot use your customer-managed KMS for encrypted model caches today \u0014 that's Dedicated/Private territory.
[06:05] Ben: So for our use case, sensitive flows stay in Dedicated with our KMS, and non-sensitive can use Hosted as a cost-saver. We'll need clear policy controls in the console.
[06:15] Maya: Console has per-route policies, RBAC, and SSO integration (SAML). We can demo route configuration in the POC.
[06:25] Priya: On the security front, disclose the SOC2 and encryption-at-rest details please.
[06:30] Maya: Yep \u0014 I'll send the SOC2 report and our encryption + key handling docs. Note sometimes transcriptions say 'sock two' sorry for the accent \u0014 but we'll send originals.
[06:40] Priya: (laughs) Noted.
[06:45] Sofia: For Private/on-prem, what's the control plane footprint? We want to avoid big ops overhead.

[06:52] Liam: Private has a lightweight customer-managed control plane with an optional air-gapped package; we ship terraform modules and ops runbook. Ops overhead is similar to a standard k8s-managed inference stack; we provide support for deployment and upgrade automation.
[07:10] Ben: How often do upgrades require restarts of running pods? We need rolling upgrades with zero downtime for sessions.

[07:18] Liam: Our runtime supports graceful draining: KV cache snapshotting and warm-starts. For canary rollouts we route a small percentage, run validation, then shift traffic. For stateful session restarts we recommend sticky routing with session handover grace period.
[07:35] Priya: Can you show an example policy for failover?

[07:40] Liam: Sure I can share a sample YAML policy: primary region us-east-1, secondary us-west-2, fallback model order: rwd-v2, rwd-v2-quant, rwd-v1-small; degrade thresholds: latency>500ms for 30s or error rate>5% triggers failover. We'll attach this to the POC docs.
[07:58] Priya: The 'rwd' names are Red wood shorthand? Sometimes anglos mis-hear Redwood as 'red wood' in our notes, ha.
[08:05] Maya: Totally \u0014 common transcript issue. We'll make docs with explicit names and version hashes.
[08:12] Ben: For billing during POC, do you charge for cross-region egress?
[08:16] Maya: There can be network egress charges depending on deployment; for POC we typically absorb costs for a short trial if it's a committed evaluation. We'll note it in the POC scope.
[08:30] Priya: Our legal team will ask about audit logs and who has access to them.

[08:35] Liam: We provide per-request tracing, token-level cost breakdown, and immutable audit logs you can forward to your SIEM. You control retention for Private and Dedicated; Hosted has configurable retention tiers.
[08:50] Sofia: Retention needs to be 13 months for compliance \u0014 is that possible?
[08:55] Maya: Yes, with Dedicated + add-on observability retention we can meet that.
[09:02] Priya: If a region is flapping, do you do automatic circuit breaking to stop hitting that region?
[09:08] Liam: Yes, circuit-breakers prevent retry storms. You can configure thresholds and cool-down windows. The system will stop routing to unhealthy regions and send alerts.
[09:20] Ben: Alerts \u0014 how do we get them? PagerDuty, webhooks, email?
[09:24] Liam: All of the above. Also Slack integrations and tracing links for fail events.
[09:30] Priya: One more \u0014 model quantization during fallback: what's the latency impact vs quality delta?

[09:36] Liam: Quantized variants are usually 20-40% faster with slight perf drop; depends on workload. We can run evals on your prompts and measure ROUGE/BLEU or custom metrics. We recommend a canary stage where 5-10% traffic hits quantized model and we evaluate quality metrics.
[09:55] Sofia: We'll provide labeled prompt sets and acceptance thresholds.

[10:00] Maya: Perfect. Let's outline the POC: 1) define traffic profile and success criteria, 2) pick regions (us-east/us-west), 3) spin up Dedicated cluster with cross-region cache replication, 4) run failover sim and measure p95/p99 and quality metrics.
[10:18] Priya: Sounds good. For the POC, can Redwood help with tooling to simulate region failover?
[10:22] Liam: Yes, we have a fault-injection harness and synthetic traffic generator we can share. We'll run the first simulation with you and then hand over scripts.
[10:32] Ben: On data residency \u0014 some shipments include EU personal data. We'll need region restriction to EU for those flows. How granular can routing be?
[10:40] Liam: Per-route and per-tenant controls. You can annotate requests and route by metadata. There's also tagging and policy-driven routing in the console.
[10:50] Priya: Great. Anything else we should be aware of operationally?

[10:55] Maya: Rolling upgrades, monitoring, runbooks \u0014 we'll provide an SRE playbook with steps for failover, rollback, and root-cause. Also, we'll recommend SLOs and alert thresholds tailored to your traffic.
[11:08] Sofia: For encryption \u0014 can we bring our own HSM?
[11:12] Liam: Yes for Private and Dedicated we support BYOK via customer KMS/HSM integrations and key rotation policies. Hosted cannot use customer HSM for now.
[11:22] Ben: What about cold-starts for models \u0014 if we route to another region model has to load, how do you prevent large latency spikes?
[11:30] Liam: We use warm pool instances and pre-warming heuristics based on traffic forecasts. For Dedicated you can reserve warm pools and set model pinning to keep critical models resident.
[11:45] Priya: For our highest-priority flows we want pinned models in each region.
[11:50] Maya: Noted \u0014 we'll size Dedicated accordingly in the proposal.
[11:58] Priya: Any compliance concerns with sending PII to Hosted as overflow? We prefer to avoid that entirely.
[12:04] Maya: Then hybrid routing should enforce strict metadata tags so PII never leaves Dedicated/Private. We'll document the policy and show console enforcement in the demo.
[12:18] Ben: Ok, next \u0014 who will be the technical leads on the POC from both sides?
[12:24] Priya: I'll be exec sponsor; Ben will be infra lead; Sofia will own model validation. From Redwood, Maya and Liam?
[12:30] Maya: Yes, that works. We'll cc solutions engineering and support.
[12:36] Priya: Timeline \u0014 can you share a draft SOW and pricing for Dedicated?
[12:40] Liam: We'll send draft sizing and pricing within a week. For pricing we need traffic profile and target regions which you'll supply.
[12:50] Sofia: Quick clarification \u0014 if the Dedicated cluster hits capacity and we overflow to Hosted for non-sensitive traffic, how do you reconcile billing and quotas?
[12:58] Maya: The console shows per-route breakdown by model, region, and cost. We can attribute overflow usage separately and include that in billing reconciliation.
[13:10] Priya: Great. Anything else on fallback SLAs?

[13:15] Liam: On contract we can include credits for availability misses; falling back to a quantized model does not generally trigger SLA credits unless it was part of an outage. We'll be explicit in the SOW about allowed graceful degradation modes.
[13:30] Ben: We'll review that with procurement. Legal will want the exact definitions of 'availability' vs 'degraded performance'.
[13:38] Maya: Sure \u0014 we'll provide contract language examples and an SLA appendix.
[13:45] Priya: Anything we should test specifically in the POC beyond latency and quality?
[13:50] Sofia: I'd add session handover correctness, cache consistency, and key rotation during active sessions.
[13:58] Liam: Good call \u0014 we can simulate key rotation in a safe test harness.
[14:05] Maya: Let's recap action items and next steps...

[14:10] Maya: 1) Maya sends SOC2 & security pack; 2) Liam shares Dedicated sizing and preliminary pricing; 3) Aurelia shares traffic profile and labeled prompt set; 4) schedule POC kickoff next week. Anything to add?
[14:25] Priya: Add: confirm KMS/HSM constraints. We'll also share legal's procurement timeline.
[14:32] Ben: I'll start drafting the infra playbook and will sync with Liam offline.
[14:38] Sofia: I'll prepare the evaluation suite for quality checks.
[14:44] Maya: Great. We'll aim to have docs and SOW draft by 2026-04-06. I'll follow up in email with the links. Any final questions?
[14:55] Priya: No more questions. Appreciate the thoroughness.
[15:00] Maya: Thanks everyone \u0014 we'll follow up. Meeting end.
[15:05] Call ended
